entry.title: 3B1B Neural Networks: Part 1
entry.content:
Neural Networks

Part 1 of my notes on the 3B1B Neural Network series

Neurons and activation

  • A neuron holds a number — the activation. High activation = the neuron “lights up”.
  • With sigmoid, activation lands in [0,1]. That range is a property of the activation function, not of neurons in general — modern networks mostly use ReLU, where activations are unbounded above.
  • More precisely, a neuron isn’t a stored number — it’s a function. It takes the activations of the previous layer and spits out its own activation. The entire network is likewise one big function.
  • So an activation only exists while data flows forward; nothing is kept between inferences. (During training they are cached, because backprop needs them.)
  • Loosely analogous to brain neurons, but the mapping is weak: biological neurons fire discrete spikes, so an activation is closer to a firing rate than to a neuron’s state.

Network shape (MNIST)

  • Input: 28×28 = 784 pixels → 784 input neurons, one per pixel, value encoding brightness.
  • Input values sit in [0,1] because brightness is normalized (0–255 divided by 255) during pre-processing.
  • Output: 10 neurons, one per digit; activation = how strongly the network thinks the image is that digit. These are in [0,1] because of sigmoid, and they do not sum to 1 — they aren’t probabilities. (Softmax is what gives you a probability distribution.)
  • This model: 2 hidden layers, 16 neurons each — picked arbitrarily, for the visuals.
  • Every neuron in a layer connects to every neuron in the next — indicating how each activation influences the next layer’s activations. Some connections are stronger than others.

Why layers might work

  • Hope: each hidden neuron fires on a subcomponent — e.g. the loop or the stroke that make up a 9.
  • Layer 2 neurons ≈ specific edges → layer 3 neurons ≈ larger-scale patterns → output neuron ≈ the digit.
  • Same shape in speech: raw audio → distinct sounds → syllables → words.
  • This is the motivating story, not what the trained network actually does. When you inspect the learned weights of this network, they look close to random noise rather than clean edge detectors.

Weights and bias

  • To make a layer-2 neuron fire on a particular edge: give positive weights to the input neurons at the edge’s pixels, and negative weights to surrounding pixels, so the neuron fires on an edge rather than a blob.
  • A weight is a learned multiplier on a previous-layer activation. Positive → previous neuron being on pushes this one on; negative → pushes it off.
  • Activation = weighted sum of previous activations, plus bias, squished into [0,1] by sigmoid (logistic curve): very negative → ~0, very positive → ~1. So a' = σ(w·a + b).
  • The weighted sum itself has no bounds, which is why the squishing is needed.
  • Bias shifts the input to sigmoid, moving where the neuron starts to care. Effectively −b is the threshold the weighted sum must clear before the neuron is meaningfully active. Positive bias = easier to activate, negative = harder.
  • In short: weighted sum = what pattern the neuron picks up on; bias = how big that sum must be before the neuron fires.

Q&A

  • Why do MNIST digits have to be centered? Is there similar pre-processing for other CNN-based models — is it CNN-specific or does it extend to Transformers?
    • The network has no translation invariance. Each input pixel is mapped to a fixed weight for a fixed input neuron. If a digit, let’s say “7” is shifted 5px, it lights up a completely different set of neurons than the ones the network learned to associate with “7”, so it fails. Centering/normalizing removes that variance. CNNs reduce this need, because convolution + shared weights give some translation invariance. Transformers on raw pixels still need position handling (patches + positional embeddings), but it doesn’t need centering the way a plain MLP does. Attention can relate any patch to any patch regardless of position.
  • How can the brain identify digits with almost no compute or time, while computers need so much power and possibly training time for the same task? What’s the difference?
    • Out of scope for this blog. Stay tuned :)
  • Why pick 2 hidden layers of 16 neurons? What’s the actual criteria for choosing hyperparameters — depth and width?
    • There’s no formula to say the optimal depth and width for a network for a task. It’s an emperical search, same as the arbitrary 2x16 in this lesson. Start from the known good architectures for the problem domain, and tune via experimentation. More capacity until the validation performance stops improving or starts overfitting.
  • Why this specific structure (fully-connected layers) for a neural network?
    • A fully connected layer assumes nothing about the relationship between the variables. Every input neuron connects to every output neuron with an independent weight. If you have no prior knowledge of which pixels interacts with which, a fully connected layer allows the network to learn arbitrary interactions from scratch. Also mathematically, a feed forward network with a non-linear activation functions is a universal function approximator.
  • Why do we need bias at all?
    • Just like the intercept (+c) in the linear equation y = mx + c, the bias shifts the decision boundary or activation function up, down, left or right. Without bias, every neuron’s decision boundary is forced through the origin (w·a = 0).

References

  • Neural networks — 3Blue1Brown

entry.title: Anyone Dread: The Selfless I
entry.content:
What if some day or night a demon were to steal after you into your loneliest loneliness, and say to you, “This life as you now live it and have lived it, will be completed erased, and there will be no evidence of your existence, every pain and every joy and every thought and sigh and everything unutterably small or great in your life will be erased, all gone with the wind, and replaced by a random identity, a random life, a random family, and random memories” Would you not throw yourself down and gnash your teeth and curse the demon who thus spoke? Or would a sudden, icy dread wash over you as the demon smiles and whispers: “Why do you tremble? Are you so certain we have not already made this deal, and the life you now live is simply the one you drew blindly from the dark?”

The presentation was inspired after Nietzsche’s Eternal Recurrence.

How is choosing a random life any different from being born? I call this thought experiment “Anyone dread”, it’s a simple fact that the conscious you (ego) could have been anyone, like someone who’s in great joy at having hiked a huge mountain, or someone who’s at complete peace after receiving a hug from their loved one, or someone who’s in deep pain after unluckily getting his legs broken and being crippled for life, or someone who died at the very first bullets from the enemy on the other side, who promised to his wife and children that he would come back home. It’s strange because they experienced it just the same way you would have experienced it if it were you. And the strangest fact is, for them, it is “you”.

When you strip away the boundaries of the self, the sheer amount of suffering in this world, suddenly feels intensely personal. But the same doesn’t hold for joy in this world, does it? I called it Anyone Dread for a reason, because you feel more dread rather than joy at the prospect of a random life. So does that mean we’re just more prone to feel dread more than joy or that there is more suffering in the world? The former makes sense to me through evolutionary reasonings, but I don’t have an answer for the latter. This awful dreadful feeling is driven by empathy, in this particular case — Universal empathy. It scares you because you recognize the reality of other people’s suffering, and realize that fundamentally, the consciousness experiencing that pain is the same as yours.

Now entertain this thought experiment in the style of Rawls’, imagine if there was just the God, and you. The God comes to you as says, “I’m going to lend you a bit of my power, the power to create a human society in the planet called Earth, however you wish. But after you create the society, you will be transformed into a normal random human being who will be part of the same society as everyone else. How would you build the society?” Now wouldn’t you build a society which has the least probability of anyone suffering unnecessarily. It is because you could be anyone, it is in our best interest to minimize the unnecessarily suffering for everyone (unnecessary suffering because the growth, meaning behind necessary suffering is whole another topic). Although in reality, you have limited power and time, but the logic of changing the world for better still applies. You want the world to be better for the future generation than what you were served. I imagine every parent experiencing a feeling akin to this when their child is born. But there is another solution to this immense suffering; wipe out all consciousness, so there’s no suffering. But consciousness is rarer than black holes, and there might be something valuable about it to just throw away without care.

The truth right now is, you were assigned this life, or rather born into it. Born to a certain pair of parents, in a specific body and environment. That can’t be changed, but you are still an agent in this world. You still have control over how your life, and how you can change and adapt in the sands of time (ignoring the physics argument of free will). The randomness is precisely what makes this life irreplaceable. You didn’t earn it, you didn’t choose it, but this is the one you got. The fact that your “I” can’t be changed anymore, that this is all you’ll get to experience the reality as, makes you accept both the good and bad, your past, your present, and open handedly welcome the future. Essentially the crux of Amor fati. This makes your life all the more important (especially to you).

entry.title: Wu Wei: Conscious and the Unconscious

link.title: Wu Wei: Conscious and the Unconscious

entry.content:
Wu Wei is a foundational concept in the Daoist philosophy, and translates to “effortless action”, “actionless action” or you can say it’s the Art of doing nothing. Well that doesn’t mean you should be lazy and slack off, but instead it’s about aligning your life in a way that things feel effortless. It can also be called the flow state.

In any areas of life in which we want to get efficient or good at, we should let the unconscious mind handle it. Be it driving, sports, writing, dancing, even math for that matter. Take for example when you are learning to ride a motorcycle, you need to be aware of the speed, the gear shifting, clutch, breaking, and all the while managing balance. But after you learn, you can easily navigate traffic while ranting about the GTA 6 release date on a phone call. This reminds me of a proverb in Kannada, “ಕಲಿಯೋ ತನಕ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ವಿದ್ಯೆ, ಕಲಿತ ಮೇಲೆ ಕೋತಿ ವಿದ್ಯೆ” (Kaliyo tanaka brahma vidye, kalita mele kapi vidye). Translates to (“Until you learn it, it’s divine knowledge; once you learn it, it’s monkey business.”) That’s the effortless action, you’re not demanding your conscious mind to do a certain task, it just happens automatically.

Note: I’m using ‘unconscious’ loosely to mean the automatic, non-deliberate processing.

When this is applied on more than just activities or tasks, but rather on career, entrepreneurship, profession or any long term endeavor, I’d like to call it, Eventual Wu Wei. Naval said, “Do what feels like play to you, but like work to others”. But it would be a mistake to assume you’ll immediately feel it like play. Some are driven by extrinsic motivation, or a need to prove something, or have no other choice. But if you keep practicing it, and if it energizes you instead of draining, and you start getting good at it, it is play and you’ve achieved eventual wu wei. Well it’s not the case that you’ll be in continuous flow state thereafter. The point is you won’t feel like you’re fighting your mind to solve a problem, you’ll be fighting the problem. You could argue, “If it feels like playing, what if I get bored of it? What then?”. Maybe boredom is the signal that you’ve mastered the current level and the unconscious needs a harder problem to chew on. Or maybe the play was always extrinsic and you fooled yourself.

So how do we get our unconscious mind to take over the wheel? Practice is the only key to delegate stuff to the unconscious. You can’t consciously force yourself to feel joy in something or be good at it, but only the conscious mind can do the training. Wu Wei can be achieved by having both of the conscious and the unconscious minds working hand in hand towards a goal. The conscious mind trains the unconscious mind to change and update (essentially hard-wiring in the brain), while the unconscious mind plays the game efficiently. That is practice. That is learning. That is the work.

It’s true that you can apply Wu Wei on the path to stupid addictions which might be easier than you think. When you’ve trained your unconscious mind on the wrong thing (by your own definition), you have essentially developed a bad habit. Like reaching out to your phone to open Twitter seconds after closing it, even when you know well enough you should be working for the meeting tomorrow. But as with all learning (or unlearning if you will) requires time and effort. So initially, retraining will feel like a chore, even painful sometimes, but that’s the point. Of course, it’ll be hard.

I think that many of the meaning-related problems humans face is because our conscious mind is not aligned with our unconscious mind that evolution shaped, or at least we haven’t spent enough time on it to adapt. Joscha Bach’s view of consciousness is that it was born out of the need to solve hard problems in survival. So in a way consciousness is not suffering, it’s the solution to suffering. Consciousness made us aware of our own shortcomings and weakness, so that we can work towards improvement through the use of tools and creations. Consciousness is evolution’s gift for improving ourselves on a timescale evolution itself can’t match. But of course too much of self-consciousness is not good either, it’ll turn you into an overwhelmed philosopher.
